correctness.rationale: Corner maximization replaces each half-side h_i by h_i+|t_i| for center t; centering preserves feasibility and volume. For positive squared half-sides the log-product is strictly concave. The three-equality solution has W≥U≥V>0 for β≤γ<α+β, so the first two multipliers are positive. The third is (1/U+1/W−1/V)/2, equals 1/(2W)>0 at γ=β, and decreases strictly to negative infinity. Its unique zero satisfies 1/V=1/(α−V)+1/(β−V), which has one solution in (0,α) since the left side decreases strictly and the right side increases strictly from finite values to infinity. It is the smaller quadratic root v*. The proof’s other root is at or above α (equal when α=β), not strictly above in the equality case; it is still excluded. The two-first-equalities candidate has supporting multipliers (1/U,1/W,0) and is feasible exactly when γ≥α+β−2v*. In both branches the supporting-plane inequality and strict concavity give the unique triple, and the two saturated cylinder inequalities force all center offsets to vanish. The maximum of x²+z² over the first two cylinders is α+β at y=0, and scaling that maximizing point gives witnesses between any two third squared radii below redundancy. Thus contact ends strictly earlier, not merely at a redundant constraint. For log-volume f, f′ equals half the third multiplier below the threshold and zero above; f″ from the left is −(U⁻²+V⁻²+W⁻²)/8 and is zero from the right, so the second derivative at the threshold does not exist. A separate rational replay at α=β=1 and γ=6/5,4/3,3/2 recovered the active multipliers, the plateau volume 16/(3√3), and the left curvature −27/16. At γ=3/2, x²=z²=7/8 and y=0 witnesses nonredundancy. These are bounded checks, not the global proof; the uploaded script was read, not executed.
residual_risks: The result is for axis-parallel boxes and for variation in the squared radius γ with fixed α,β; it does not extend the smoothness claim across permutations or to rotated boxes.
